From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference>

Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Commercial onboarding: PO vs corporate card & marketplace interest — Novex AI

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has a clear path: 

Key notes from our discovery:
- Expected annual run rate for the pilot: ~$95k (projected over 12 months)
- Primary question from your finance team: do we need a PO for vendor enablement, or can Novex use corporate card payments?
- Novex is evaluating whether to onboard via the AWS Marketplace/GCP Marketplace or via direct vendor setup (vendor onboarding process required for PO).

Open items / asks for procurement:
1) Does Novex require a purchase order to start a pilot or is a corporate card acceptable for initial invoices? (If PO, please share preferred PO template)
2) Who should we engage in Procurement (name + email) to start vendor onboarding?
3) Any specific vendor onboarding docs or security attestations we should prep (W9, tax forms, SOC 2 evidence)?
4) Desired billing cadence: monthly invoices vs net30/45/60 terms?

Attachments: postcall-notes.txt (brief internal notes from today's call).

Proposed next steps:
- If PO required: we can provide vendor-setup-form.xlsx and SOW-draft.pdf to speed procurement intake.
- If card allowed: we can provision early access under a short T&C and invoice monthly.
- I can schedule a 30-min handoff with procurement if you introduce the contact.

Would you be able to confirm procurement preference and, if PO is required, who to loop in?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into your intake pipeline.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie — good summary. A few quick answers from procurement: 

- For anything above $50k/year we prefer a PO and invoice flow; under that threshold corporate card is often acceptable for pilot spend.
- I'll introduce Elena Martinez (cc'd) who owns vendor setup and onboarding — she will confirm exact docs we need.
- We are open to Marketplace onboarding (AWS) but procurement may still require vendor setup if they need our tax/insurance records on file. Marketplace can speed payments but doesn't always remove vendor intake for our legal/compliance needs.
- Billing cadence: preferred monthly invoices, net30.

Elena, can you advise what vendor forms you need from Redwood? If you prefer, Stephanie, send the vendor setup form and SOW and I can push to procureops.

Looping in from a delivery/vendor-ops perspective — quick note on what speeds procurement: 

1) Vendor-setup-form.xlsx (attached) — completed by vendors typically becomes the core of our AP intake. If Elena can confirm fields required on her side, we can pre-fill portions (tax id, payment remit, primary contact).
2) SOW-draft.pdf (attached) — provides the commercial and scope language procurement needs to route approvals. If Novex needs custom language (privacy, data residency), flag now so legal can prepare.
3) Marketplace vs direct vendor: Marketplace enrollment usually reduces procurement friction for payment processing, but most customers still request our W9 and SOC 2 link in their vendor record. If Novex wants to avoid vendor setup entirely we can provision a short pilot on card and switch to PO later, but that requires an acceptance of our standard pilot terms.

Questions for Elena / procureops: 
- Any non-standard fields (risk codes, tax forms) we should include in the vendor form?
- Preferred invoice remittance address and contact for AP?

Proposed action: Stephanie to send the vendor-setup-form.xlsx and SOW-draft.pdf to Elena; Elena to confirm whether a PO and vendor creation are required before the first invoice. If PO required, we should aim for vendor record creation within 7 business days.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.inference
